##Target Damage-seq

## CPD_COMBINED

```{r CPD}

library(dplyr)
# Read BED file into a data frame
CPD_gene_normalized <- read.table("CPD_Enrichment.bed", header = FALSE, sep = "\t")

# Rename columns
colnames(CPD_gene_normalized) <- c("chr", "start", "end", "name", "CPD_density", "Cluster_length", "CPD_Enrichment")



```

## Mutation_COMBINED_RPKM
```{r}
library(dplyr)
# Read BED file into a data frame
Mutation_normalized <- read.table("CPD_Cluster_Mutation_counts.bed", header = FALSE, sep = "\t")

# Rename columns
colnames(Mutation_normalized) <- c("chr", "start", "end", "name", "count")

# Calculate gene length in kilobases
Mutation_normalized <- Mutation_normalized %>%
  mutate(gene_length = (end - start))

# Calculate the total number of reads across the dataset
total_reads_Mutation <- sum(Mutation_normalized$count)

# Calculate RPKM for each cluster
Mutation_normalized <- Mutation_normalized %>%
  mutate(MELA_CPKM = (count * 1e6) / (gene_length/1e3 * total_reads_Mutation))

#head(CPD_gene_normalized)

# Assuming CPD_gene_normalized is already loaded
# Sort based on chr, start, end, and name
Mutation_normalized <-Mutation_normalized %>%
  arrange(chr, start, end, name)
```





```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

# Merge the two data frames by chr, start, end, and name
merged_plot_data_combined <- inner_join(
  CPD_gene_normalized, 
  Mutation_normalized, 
  by = c("chr", "start", "end", "name")  # Specify the columns to merge on
)


# Create the scatter plot with linear regression line
ggplot(merged_plot_data_combined, aes(x = CPD_Enrichment, y = MELA_CPKM)) +
  geom_point(color = "#9EAAE0", size = 3, alpha = 0.7) +  
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "#F3E065", size = 2) + 
  labs(title = "CPD Correlation",
       x = "CPD Enrichment",
       y = "CPKM in MELA") +
  # Uncomment the following lines to limit x or y axes if needed

  #ylim(0, 480) +  
  theme_classic() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 16, face = "bold"), 
    axis.title.x = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),  
    axis.title.y = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),  
    axis.text = element_text(size = 12)  
  )


```

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

# Merge the two data frames
merged_plot_data_combined <- inner_join(
  CPD_gene_normalized, 
  Mutation_normalized, 
  by = c("chr", "start", "end", "name")
)

# ---- Pearson correlation + p-value ----
cor_result <- cor.test(merged_plot_data_combined$CPD_Enrichment,
                       merged_plot_data_combined$MELA_CPKM,
                       method = "pearson")

r_val <- round(cor_result$estimate, 3)
p_val <- signif(cor_result$p.value, 3)

cor_label <- paste0("Pearson r = ", r_val, "\n", "p = ", p_val)

# ---- Plot with annotation ----
 
ggplot(merged_plot_data_combined, aes(x = CPD_Enrichment, y = MELA_CPKM)) +
  geom_point(color = "#9EAAE0", size = 4, alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "#F3E065", size = 2) +
  annotate("text", x = Inf, y = Inf, label = cor_label,
           hjust = 1.1, vjust = 1.5, size = 5, fontface = "bold") +
  labs(title = "Cluster Correlation",
       x = "CPD Enrichment (RPB)",
       y = "MELA Mutation (CPKM)") +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 16, face = "bold"), 
    axis.title.x = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),  
    axis.title.y = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),  
    axis.text = element_text(size = 12),
    panel.border = element_rect(colour = "black", fill = NA, linewidth = 1.2)  # <-- add box
  )


```

##z-scale()
```{r}
library(dplyr)

# Standardize the variables (z-score normalization)
z_gene_diff <- merged_plot_data_combined %>%
  mutate(
    z_CPD = scale(CPD_Enrichment),                       # Z-score for CPD RPKM
    z_MELA = scale(MELA_CPKM)                    # Z-score for mutation RPKGCM
  )



```



```{r}
library(ggplot2)

# Create the scatter plot with centered axes
ggplot(z_gene_diff, aes(x = z_CPD, y = z_MELA)) +
  geom_point(color = "#9EAAE0", size = 3, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "#F3E065", size = 1.2) +
  labs(
    title = "Z-Score Correlation Between CPD (RPKM) and Mutation (RPKGCM)",
    x = "Z-Score of CPD Erichment)",
    y = "Z-Score of CPKM (Mutation)"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-5, 7), expand = c(0, 0.5)) +  # Adjust x-axis limits
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(-5, 7), expand = c(0, 0.5)) +  # Adjust y-axis limits
  theme_classic() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.4, size = 13, face = "bold"),
    axis.title.x = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    axis.title.y = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 12),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "gray90", size = 0.2)
  ) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "black", size = 0.8) +  # Add a horizontal line at y=0
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "black", size = 0.8)    # Add a vertical line at x=0


```


```{r}
thr <- 0.5  # size of the muted center square

z_gene_diff <- z_gene_diff %>%
  mutate(
    quadrant = case_when(
      z_CPD > 0 & z_MELA > 0 ~ "Mutation High, CPD High",       # top-right
      z_CPD > 0 & z_MELA <  0 ~ "Mutation Low, CPD High",        # bottom-right
      z_CPD <=  0 & z_MELA > 0 ~ "Mutation High, CPD Low",        # top-left
      z_CPD <=  0 & z_MELA <=  0 ~ "Mutation Low, CPD Low"          # bottom-left
    )
  )

ggplot(z_gene_diff, aes(x = z_CPD, y = z_MELA, color = quadrant)) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = -thr, xmax = thr, ymin = -thr, ymax = thr,
           fill = "grey85", alpha = 0.5, color = NA) +
  geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "black", size = 1.2) +
  labs(
    title = "Z-Score Correlation Between CPD Enrichment and Mutation (CPKM)",
    x = "Z-Score of CPD Enrichment",
    y = "Z-Score of CPKM (Mutation)"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-5, 5), expand = c(0, 0.5)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(-5, 15), expand = c(0, 0.5)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(
    "Mutation High, CPD High" = "#F28C9D",
    "Mutation Low, CPD High"  = "#F3E065",
    "Mutation High, CPD Low"  = "#65C9F3",
    "Mutation Low, CPD Low"   = "#9EAAE0"
  )) +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.6, size = 12, face = "bold"),
```

```{r}
# ========================
# Donut plot for classification
# ========================
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

# 1) Create data (replace with your actual table if needed)
df <- tribble(
  ~detailed_classification, ~count,
  "Mutation High, CPD High", 212,
  "Mutation High, CPD Low", 245,
  "Mutation Low, CPD Low", 508,
  "Mutation Low, CPD High", 397

)

# 2) Compute percentages and positions
df <- df %>%
  mutate(
    fraction = count / sum(count),
    ymax = cumsum(fraction),
    ymin = c(0, head(ymax, n = -1)),
    label = paste0(detailed_classification, " (", count, ")")
  )

# 3) Define colors (adjust if needed)
custom_colors <- c(
  "Mutation High, CPD High" = "#F28C9D",
  "Mutation Low, CPD High" = "#65C9F3",
  "Mutation High, CPD Low" = "#F3E065",
  "Mutation Low, CPD Low" = "#9EAAE0"
)

# 4) Plot
p <- ggplot(df) +
  geom_rect(aes(
    ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax,
    xmin = 2, xmax = 4,
    fill = detailed_classification
  ), color = "black") +
  coord_polar(theta = "y") +
  xlim(0, 4) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = custom_colors) +
  theme_void(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    legend.title = element_blank(),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 12),
    legend.position = "right"
  ) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 5))) +
  labs(title = "Group")

print(p)

```






```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)

# Select columns to include in BED files
selected_cols <- c("chr", "start", "end", "name", "CPD_Enrichment", "MELA_CPKM")

output_dir <- "./"
# Write each quadrant to its own BED file
quadrants <- unique(z_gene_diff$quadrant)

for (q in quadrants) {
  # Filter by quadrant
  subset_data <- z_gene_diff %>% filter(quadrant == q) %>% select(all_of(selected_cols))
  
  # Define output file name
  output_file <- paste0(output_dir, "/", gsub(" ", "_", q), ".bed")
  
  # Write to file
  write.table(subset_data, output_file, sep="\t", row.names=FALSE, col.names=FALSE, quote=FALSE)
  
  # Print confirmation message
  cat("Saved:", output_file, "\n")
}

cat("All quadrant BED files have been created.\n")
```







```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)   # <-- needed for pivot_wider

df_matrix <- z_gene_diff %>%
  mutate(CPD_Enrichment = ifelse(is.na(CPD_Enrichment), 0, CPD_Enrichment)) %>%  # Replace NAs with 0 first
  group_by(name, quadrant) %>%
  summarise(mean_CPD = mean(CPD_Enrichment), .groups = "drop") %>%  # Now compute mean
  pivot_wider(names_from = quadrant, values_from = mean_CPD) %>%
  as.data.frame()

# Replace NAs with 0 (or use the median)
df_matrix[is.na(df_matrix)] <- 0  # Option 1: Replace NAs with 0
# df_matrix[is.na(df_matrix)] <- apply(df_matrix, 1, median, na.rm = TRUE)  # Option 2: Replace NAs with median

# Set row names to gene names
rownames(df_matrix) <- df_matrix$name
df_matrix$name <- NULL  # Remove the gene name column

# Convert to matrix
df_matrix <- as.matrix(df_matrix)




```






```{r}
# Load necessary libraries
library(dplyr)

# Convert data from wide to long format for testing
df_long <- df_matrix %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  tibble::rownames_to_column("Gene") %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -Gene, names_to = "Quadrant", values_to = "CPD_Enrichment")
kruskal_result <- kruskal.test(CPD_Enrichment ~ Quadrant, data = df_long)
print(kruskal_result)

#Since the Kruskal-Wallis test is significant, we should run pairwise Wilcoxon tests to see which groups differ:
pairwise.wilcox.test(df_long$CPD_Enrichment, df_long$Quadrant, p.adjust.method = "fdr")



```


##iNDENPENDENT TEST

```{r}
library(coin)

# Convert Quadrant to a factor (important for coin package)
df_long$Quadrant <- as.factor(df_long$Quadrant)

# Perform the Asymptotic General Independence Test
ind_test_result <- independence_test(CPD_Enrichment ~ Quadrant, data = df_long, teststat = "quad")
#This test is similar to the Kruskal-Wallis test but is a generalized independence test.
#Chi-squared = 126.03 and df = 3 indicate the test statistic.
#p-value < 2.2e-16 confirms strong evidence of differences between groups.


# Extract test statistics
chi_sq_value <- round(statistic(ind_test_result)[1], 2)  # Chi-square value
p_value <- format.pval(pvalue(ind_test_result))  # Format p-value

# Raincloud plot with test results in top-right corner
ggplot(df_long, aes(x = Quadrant, y = CPD_Enrichment, fill = Quadrant, color = Quadrant)) +
  # Half-violin plot (density distribution)
  ggdist::stat_halfeye(
    adjust = 0.5,  # Smoothness
    justification = -0.2,  # Shift to left
    .width = 0,
    point_colour = NA
  ) +
  # Boxplot (for median and IQR)
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.2, outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.5, color = "black") +
  # Jittered points (for individual gene values)
  geom_jitter(width = 0.1, alpha = 0.7, size = 1) +
  # Add Independence Test Result as a text annotation (top-right corner)
  annotate("text", x = 5.5, y = max(df_long$CPD_Enrichment) * 0.9, 
           label = paste("Independence Test:\nChi² =", chi_sq_value, 
                         "\nP =", p_value),
           size = 4, hjust = 1, fontface = "bold", color = "black") +
  # Labels and theme
  labs(title = "Raincloud Plot of RPKM Across Groups with Independence Test",
       x = "",
       y = "RPKM") +
  theme_minimal() + 
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Mutation High, CPD High" = "#F28C9D", 
                               "Mutation High, CPD Low" = "#65C9F3C9", 
                               "Mutation Low, CPD High" = "#F3E065", 
                               "Mutation Low, CPD Low" = "#9EAAE0")) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Mutation High, CPD High" = "#F28C9D", 
                                "Mutation High, CPD Low" = "#65C9F3C9", 
                                "Mutation Low, CPD High" = "#F3E065", 
                                "Mutation Low, CPD Low" = "#9EAAE0")) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))  # Rotate x-axis labels for readability

```


```{r}
# Load required libraries
library(ggplot2)
library(gghalves)
library(ggdist)
library(ggpubr)  # For stat_compare_means
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

# --- 1) Long format with desired order ---
df_long <- df_matrix %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  tibble::rownames_to_column("Gene") %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -Gene, names_to = "Quadrant", values_to = "CPD_Enrichment") %>%
  mutate(
    Quadrant = factor(
      Quadrant,
      levels = c(
        "Mutation High, CPD High",
        "Mutation Low, CPD High",
        "Mutation High, CPD Low",
        "Mutation Low, CPD Low"
      )
    )
  )


# Define the pairwise comparisons
comparisons <- list(
  c("Mutation High, CPD High", "Mutation Low, CPD High"),
  c("Mutation High, CPD High", "Mutation High, CPD Low"),
  c("Mutation High, CPD High", "Mutation Low, CPD Low"),
  c("Mutation Low, CPD High", "Mutation High, CPD Low"),
  c("Mutation Low, CPD High", "Mutation Low, CPD Low"),
  c("Mutation High, CPD Low", "Mutation Low, CPD Low")
)

# Create raincloud plot with boxplot on top
ggplot(df_long, aes(x = Quadrant, y = CPD_Enrichment, fill = Quadrant, color = Quadrant)) +
  
  # Half-violin plot
  ggdist::stat_halfeye(
    adjust = 0.5,
    justification = -0.2,
    .width = 0,
    point_colour = NA
  ) +
  
  # Jittered points
  geom_jitter(width = 0.1, alpha = 0.7, size = 1) +
  
  # 👉 Boxplot LAST: so it’s on top
  geom_boxplot(
    width = 0.2, 
    outlier.shape = NA, 
    alpha = 1,               # Fully opaque
    color = "black",
    linewidth = 0.8          # Thicker lines for clarity
  ) +
  
  # Annotate chi-square result
  annotate("text", x = 5.5, y = max(df_long$RPKM) * 0.9, 
           label = paste("Independence Test:\nChi² =", chi_sq_value, 
                         "\nP =", p_value),
           size = 3, hjust = 1.1, vjust = -1.5, fontface = "bold", color = "black") +
  
  # Add pairwise comparison p-values
  stat_compare_means(
    comparisons = comparisons, 
    method = "wilcox.test",
    label = "p.signif",
    p.adjust.method = "fdr"
  ) +
  
  # Axes and scales
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 8)) +
  
  labs(
    title = "Gene-Level CPD Enrichment Across Mutation–CPD Groups",
    x = "Mutation–CPD Group",
    y = "CPD Enrichment (RPB)"
  ) +
  
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(
    "Mutation High, CPD High" = "#F28C9D",
    "Mutation Low, CPD High"  = "#F3E065",
    "Mutation High, CPD Low"  = "#65C9F3C9",
    "Mutation Low, CPD Low"   = "#9EAAE0"
  )) +
  
  scale_color_manual(values = c(
    "Mutation High, CPD High" = "#F28C9D",
    "Mutation Low, CPD High"  = "#F3E065",
    "Mutation High, CPD Low"  = "#65C9F3C9",
    "Mutation Low, CPD Low"   = "#9EAAE0"
  )) +
  
  theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    plot.title  = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"),
    panel.border = element_rect(color = "black", fill = NA, linewidth = 1)
  )

```









############################################################################
##Uniuqe cluster in just one group
```{r}
library(dplyr)

# Ensure z_gene_diff contains 'chr', 'start', and 'end' columns
exclusive_clusters <- z_gene_diff %>%
  group_by(name) %>%
  summarise(
    chr = first(chr),  # Take the first occurrence of chromosome
    start = first(start),  # Take the first occurrence of start position
    end = first(end),  # Take the first occurrence of end position
    unique_groups = n_distinct(quadrant),  # Count how many unique quadrants each gene appears in
    assigned_group = first(quadrant)  # Keep the first assigned group
  ) %>%
  filter(unique_groups == 1)  # Keep only genes that appear in a single quadrant

# Extract exclusive clusters for each group
exclusive_M_H_C_H <- exclusive_clusters %>% filter(assigned_group == "Mutation High, CPD High")
exclusive_M_H_C_L <- exclusive_clusters %>% filter(assigned_group == "Mutation High, CPD Low")
exclusive_M_L_C_H <- exclusive_clusters %>% filter(assigned_group == "Mutation Low, CPD High")
exclusive_M_L_C_L <- exclusive_clusters %>% filter(assigned_group == "Mutation Low, CPD Low")

# Print results
print(exclusive_M_H_C_H)  # Clusters unique to Mutation High, CPD High
print(exclusive_M_H_C_L)  # Clusters unique to Mutation High, CPD Low
print(exclusive_M_L_C_H)  # Clusters unique to Mutation Low, CPD High
print(exclusive_M_L_C_L)  # Clusters unique to Mutation Low, CPD Low


```

```{r}
  filter(detailed_classification == "Mutation Low, CPD High") %>%
  dplyr::select(chr, start, end, name, detailed_classification)

mutation_high_cpd_low <- z_gene_diff %>%
  filter(detailed_classification == "Mutation High, CPD Low") %>%
  dplyr::select(chr, start, end, name, detailed_classification)

mutation_low_cpd_low <- z_gene_diff %>%
  filter(detailed_classification == "Mutation Low, CPD Low") %>%
  dplyr::select(chr, start, end, name, detailed_classification)

# Save as BED files
write.table(mutation_high_cpd_high, "mutation_high_cpd_high.bed", sep = "\t", row.names = FALSE, col.names = FALSE, quote = FALSE)
write.table(mutation_low_cpd_high, "mutation_low_cpd_high.bed", sep = "\t", row.names = FALSE, col.names = FALSE, quote = FALSE)
write.table(mutation_high_cpd_low, "mutation_high_cpd_low.bed", sep = "\t", row.names = FALSE, col.names = FALSE, quote = FALSE)
write.table(mutation_low_cpd_low, "mutation_low_cpd_low.bed", sep = "\t", row.names = FALSE, col.names = FALSE, quote = FALSE)

```
